title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: What is the maximum area of an isosceles trapezoid that has legs of length \(1\) and one base twice as long as the other?

solutions.text:
Let the bases be \(a\) and \(2a.\) Each leg has horizontal offset \(\tfrac{a}{2},\) so the height is \(\sqrt{1-\tfrac{a^2}{4}}\) and the area is \(A=\tfrac{3a}{2}\sqrt{1-\tfrac{a^2}{4}}.\) Then \(A^2=\tfrac94\left(a^2-\tfrac{a^4}{4}\right),\) maximized when \(a^2=2.\) There the height is \(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\) and \(A=\tfrac{3\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\tfrac{3}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Drop the two heights; each leg spans a horizontal distance of \(\frac{\text{long base}-\text{short base}}{2}\)
With shorter base \(a,\) the area is \(\tfrac{3a}{2}\sqrt{1-\tfrac{a^2}{4}};\) maximize its square
